agent.finish_summary: Fixed the 'grouping alias' regression. Root cause: NameAliasMixin.get_alias() in sqlparse/sql.py found the 'AS' keyword token but never used it, falling through to a generic reverse scan that doesn't match T.Keyword-typed tokens by default. This meant aliases that are themselves SQL keywords (e.g. 'view') were not recognized, so get_alias() returned None and get_name()/grouping fell back incorrectly to the real name instead of the alias (reproducing AssertionError: assert 'sql_identifier' == 'view'). Fix: when AS is present, call self._get_first_name(kw_idx + 1, keywords=True) to scan starting right after AS with keyword matching enabled. Verified SELECT sql_identifier AS view now yields alias='view', and a wide range of other alias forms (implicit alias, dotted names, function/case/operation/comparison aliases, numeric alias, FROM foo f, WITH CTE) continue to work correctly with unchanged str() round-tripping.
